feat(deploy): connected wallet is now the agent - no custodial key

api/deploy.js rewritten to the same build/sign/submit pattern as
api/fee.js: the server builds an unsigned deploy tx from the user's own
UTxOs, the browser signs it via CIP-30, the server assembles and
submits. The connected wallet's own credential becomes agent_pkh, so
every dashboard-deployed wallet is genuinely controlled by whoever
deployed it - no shared AGENT_PRIVATE_KEY in Vercel signing on anyone's
behalf.

api/fee.js: treasuryAddress() now requires BENI_TREASURY_ADDRESS
directly instead of falling back to an address derived from
AGENT_PRIVATE_KEY (that fallback no longer makes sense once deploys
aren't custodial). BENI_TREASURY_ADDRESS must be set in Vercel for fee
payments to keep working.

dashboard.jsx: DeployModal now asks for a second wallet signature
after the fee (fee tx, then deploy tx), and its copy no longer claims
the wallet deploys with a Vercel-configured key.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(security): require agent signature on every Spend (agent_pkh)

The validator only checked spending caps, never who was allowed to spend -
anyone watching the chain could construct a valid Spend transaction and
drain a Beni wallet to themselves, up to the per-tx cap. Adds agent_pkh
to the datum and requires it in tx.extra_signatories for every Spend.

Also fixed the test suite, which had never actually run: tests/ is not
a directory Aiken scans (only lib/ and validators/), so this whole test
file was silently skipped since day one. Moved it into validators/,
extracted the validator body into a plain spend_logic() function so it's
callable from tests, and fixed two latent test bugs this exposed
(last_window_start and window_spent were computed wrong in two cases).
All 13 tests now actually execute and pass.

SDK (beni-sdk@0.1.2, published): GuardrailConfig.agentPkh required,
agentSpend adds the signer key, datum schema/CBOR updated.

Migration: reclaimed the real ADA from the old vulnerable mainnet
contract via OwnerAction and redeployed under the fixed validator.
Redeployed the Preview testnet demo wallet the same way. Dashboard
(api/deploy.js, api/agent-state.js) and the Telegram bot updated to
the new CBOR/schema and to set agent_pkh at deploy time.

harden(core): act on security/architecture/design/QA review of S+13

A four-lens review team (security, architecture, design, correctness) found
that the inbox-exit trust gate was an incomplete copy of flyway_check's,
opening a replay path, plus a real correctness bug. Incorporated:

- Cross-peer replay (security): honorInboxExit now enforces the on-disk
  placement binding — an inbox exit must sit under its sender's subtree —
  so a peer can't replay another peer's genuinely-signed exit from their own
  delivery path.
- Wrong-recipient replay (security/correctness/design): require env.to ==
  our DID, and re-check the peer-exit target == recipient invariant on read.
- Outbox authenticity (security): outbox exits are verified against our own
  DID document + placement, not trusted implicitly by location.
- Stale-exit-closes-future-agreement (design/correctness): a temporal guard
  — an exit cannot close an agreement created after it (createdAt > sentAt).
  Exit doesn't retract recognition, so re-collaboration is first-class.
- Silent typo (design): a honored project/syndicate exit matching zero
  agreements is surfaced as an advisory issue.
- Robustness (correctness): validate exit sentAt; flag unknown agreement
  state rather than echoing it; never throw on a malformed peers.yaml entry;
  refuse an inbox exit when recognizedAt is absent.

+8 status tests locking these (31 total): cross-peer + wrong-recipient
replay refused, temporal guard, syndicate close, zero-match advisory,
retroactive refused, outbox non-verification, unknown state. Full suite
green: core 318, mcp 23, cli 95, agent 9.

ADR-0013 amended: the fuller gate, the temporal/monotone-latch semantics,
and the corrected membership reasoning (the exit target is unilateral, so
the co-signature is not the defense — the zero-match advisory is). Tier 8
walkthrough updated. Deferred (tracked): extract one shared
verifyInboxSignal predicate so status and check provably can't drift.

feat(public): How It Works page rendered from JSON markdown

Add a public /how-it-works page whose content lives in JSON and is
rendered through a small, dependency-free Markdown renderer.

- data/how-it-works.json: page content as structured sections, each
body authored in Markdown (covers the swap flow, the 2 ADA refundable
fee, E2E messaging, and on-chain proofs).
- lib/markdown.tsx: renderMarkdown() turns Markdown into React elements
(headings, paragraphs, ordered/unordered lists, blockquotes, rules,
inline bold/italic/code/links). No new dependency, no
dangerouslySetInnerHTML — XSS-safe by construction.
- app/how-it-works/page.tsx: server component with a hero, sticky
table-of-contents, and the rendered article, wrapped in the public
header/footer. Public route (not gated by proxy.ts).

Nav + footer:
- Header/footer "How it Works" now links to /how-it-works; the #ledger
and #discovery anchors are made absolute (/#…) so they resolve from
any page.
- Footer: social icons moved into the links column; bottom bar now holds
only the tagline and copyright.

fix: prevent lost/duplicate ADA payouts and add test coverage for tasks.ts

Refunds that failed after a deadline closure were permanently unrecoverable, and neither approveWork nor processDeadlineRefund guarded against a concurrent/retried call sending a duplicate payout. Both now track payout/refund state independently of task/claim status via an atomic compare-and-swap lock, so failures are safely retryable and a payout's tx hash is persisted the instant it succeeds. Also sets up Vitest with an in-memory fake Supabase client and a full test suite for app/actions/tasks.ts to lock in this behavior.
